problem: Loopbreaker treats a verified behavior as verified forever. Real proof rots: a wired replay or a behavior verified against a since-changed contract can be stale, yet it still counts toward shipping. There is no notion of proof expiring or needing re-attestation.
appetite: One freshness slice over the existing evidence and verification records — the flattened part of Rordi's claim calculus, not the whole thing.
smallest_slice: Record verified_at and a decay half-life, derive a fresh/decaying/expired band in substrate(), and make ship-status treat an expired enforced behavior as not shipping-ready with a distinct reason.
non_goals: Supersession edges and the full claim evaluator model (stay in Rordi)
success_signal: An enforced behavior verified beyond its half-life reads expired, holds shipping with a verification_expired reason distinct from unverified, and recovers to fresh when re-attested.
reversibility: Default the half-life to infinite to disable decay entirely without touching the schema.

risks.risk: A too-short default half-life expires healthy work and creates churn.
risks.mitigation: Default to 90 days and make the half-life configurable per behavior.
